88 Cobblestone Arcade, Suite 400, Port Avalon

Re: Engagement for Tax Compliance and Advisory Services

Dear Ms. Quillmoor,

1. Purpose of this Letter. This letter (the "Engagement Letter") confirms the terms on which Harlow & Finch Advisory LLP (the "Firm") will provide services to the Client. It supersedes any prior proposal dated before 1 February 2025.

2. Scope of Services. The Firm will (a) prepare the Client's federal and state corporate income tax returns for the fiscal year ending 31 December 2024; (b) prepare quarterly sales tax filings for four (4) quarters; and (c) provide up to twelve (12) hours of general tax advisory consultation per calendar year (the "Advisory Hours").

3. Exclusions. The Services do not include audit or attest services, payroll processing, representation before any taxing authority in an examination, or valuation of any business interest.

4. Fees. The fixed fee for the corporate income tax returns is $6,800. Each quarterly sales tax filing is billed at $450 per filing. Advisory Hours are billed at $285 per hour, and any advisory time in excess of the Advisory Hours is billed at $325 per hour.

5. Retainer. Upon signing, the Client shall pay a retainer of $2,000, which the Firm will apply against the final invoice for the engagement. The retainer is non-refundable once work on the income tax returns has begun.

6. Invoicing and Payment. The Firm will invoice monthly in arrears. Invoices are payable within 21 days of the invoice date. Amounts unpaid after 21 days accrue interest at 1% per month on the outstanding balance, calculated from the invoice due date.

7. Expenses. Out-of-pocket expenses exceeding $150 in any single month require the Client's prior written approval.

8. Client Responsibilities. The Client shall deliver complete books and records to the Firm no later than 15 February 2025 for the income tax returns. If records are delivered after that date, the Firm does not guarantee filing by the original due date and may file an extension on the Client's behalf.

9. Term and Termination. This Engagement Letter remains in effect until the Services are complete. Either party may terminate the engagement on 30 days' written notice. If the Client terminates, the Client shall pay for all Services performed through the effective date of termination.

10. Limitation of Liability. The Firm's aggregate liability arising out of this engagement shall not exceed the total fees paid by the Client under this Engagement Letter in the 12 months preceding the claim.

11. Record Retention. The Firm will retain its working papers for seven (7) years following completion of the engagement, after which they may be destroyed without notice.

12. Governing Law. This Engagement Letter is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.

13. Entire Agreement. This Engagement Letter is the entire agreement of the parties regarding the Services and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties.

Please sign and return a copy of this letter to confirm your agreement.

Harlow & Finch Advisory LLP
By: Theodric Harlow, Managing Partner

Accepted and agreed:
Quillmoor Bakeries Inc.
By: Edwina Quillmoor, Chief Executive Officer

pages:
EXAMPLE CONSULTING AGREEMENT

This Consulting Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 10 June 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC, a limited liability company with offices at 19 Gantry Lane, Millhaven ("Consultant"), and Tessaline Outdoor Co., a corporation with offices at 640 Ridgeback Avenue, Cedar Hollow ("Company").

1. Definitions.
1.1 "Deliverables" means the reports, models and presentations described in Exhibit A.
1.2 "Project" means the market-entry assessment for the Company's proposed line of lightweight camping stoves.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Cedar Hollow.

2. Services. Consultant shall perform the Project and deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the timeline in Exhibit A. Consultant shall assign a lead consultant who will devote not less than 20 hours per week to the Project.

3. Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6) months (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter it renews automatically for successive three (3) month periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 15 Business Days before the end of the then-current term.

4. Minimum Commitment. The Company may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the first three (3) months of the Initial Term. After the third month, the Company may terminate for convenience on 20 Business Days' written notice.

5. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after receiving written notice of it.

6. Fees. The Company shall pay Consultant a monthly fee of $14,500 (the "Monthly Fee"). In addition, upon acceptance of the final Deliverable the Company shall pay a success fee equal to 4% of the first-year projected revenue stated in the accepted market-entry model, capped at $40,000.

7. Payment Terms. Consultant shall invoice the Monthly Fee on the first Business Day of each month. The Company shall pay each invoice within 30 days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month, and Consultant may suspend the Services if any invoice remains unpaid more than 45 days after receipt.

8. Expenses. The Company shall reimburse reasonable travel expenses pre-approved in writing. Airfare shall be economy class for flights under five (5) hours.

9. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of three (3) years after termination of this Agreement. This obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party.

10. Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees, all rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Company. Consultant retains ownership of its pre-existing methodologies, templates and tools, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the Deliverables.

11. Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who worked on the Project.

12. Insurance. Consultant shall maintain professional liability insurance with a limit of not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

13. Limitation of Liability. Except for breaches of Section 9, neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14. Governing Law and Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch. The courts located in Millhaven shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

15. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set out above.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC — By: Odalys Brindlewick, Principal
Tessaline Outdoor Co. — By: Marten Tessaline, President

MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (TEST DOCUMENT)

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the "NDA") is made on 2 September 2025 between Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd., registered office 7 Copperleaf Yard, Dunmarrow ("Fernwhistle"), and Plumtree Analytica GmbH, Kastanienweg 21, Ostervale ("Plumtree"). Each is a "Party" and, when disclosing, the "Discloser"; when receiving, the "Recipient".

1. Purpose. The Parties wish to evaluate a possible joint development of warehouse picking software (the "Purpose").

2. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Discloser, whether oral, written or electronic, that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Oral disclosures must be summarised in writing and marked confidential within 14 days of disclosure to be protected.

3. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public other than through breach of this NDA; (b) was known to the Recipient before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Confidential Information; or (d) is received from a third party without restriction.

4. Obligations. The Recipient shall (a) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations no less protective than this NDA; and (c) protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care.

5. Compelled Disclosure. If the Recipient is required by law to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the Discloser prompt notice, where legally permitted, so that the Discloser may seek a protective order.

6. Term. This NDA applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years following its date. The obligations in Section 4 survive for five (5) years after the last disclosure, except that obligations relating to source code survive indefinitely.

7. Return or Destruction. Within 30 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy all Confidential Information, and an officer of the Recipient shall certify destruction in writing within 10 days thereafter.

8. No Licence. Nothing in this NDA grants any licence under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right, except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

9. No Obligation. Neither Party is obliged to proceed with any transaction. Either Party may end discussions at any time by written notice.

10. Remedies. Each Party acknowledges that breach may cause irreparable harm and that the Discloser may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

11. Governing Law. This NDA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ostervale, and the courts of Dunmarrow have non-exclusive jurisdiction.

Signed for Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd.: Ines Fernwhistle, Director
Signed for Plumtree Analytica GmbH: Jurgen Pfeffer-Lind, Managing Director

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
(Example — for testing purposes)

This Master Services Agreement ("MSA") is effective 15 January 2025 between Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. ("Provider") and Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society ("Customer").

1. Definitions.
"Services" means the managed hosting, monitoring and backup services described in each Order Form.
"Order Form" means an ordering document executed by both parties that references this MSA.
"Monthly Uptime Percentage" means the total minutes in a calendar month minus minutes of Downtime, divided by the total minutes in that month.
"Downtime" means any period of more than five (5) consecutive minutes during which the production environment is unreachable, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and performed between 01:00 and 05:00 local time, not exceeding eight (8) hours per month.

2. Service Levels.
2.1 Provider shall make the production environment available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%.
2.2 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.5%, Customer will receive a credit of 5% of the monthly Services fee; below 99.5% but at least 99.0%, a credit of 10%; and below 99.0%, a credit of 25%. Service Credits in any month shall not exceed 25% of that month's fees.
2.3 Claims. Customer must request Service Credits within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for failure to meet the service levels, except as provided in Section 6.3.
2.4 Support Response. Provider shall respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes, Severity 2 incidents within 2 hours, and Severity 3 incidents within 1 Business Day.

3. Fees and Payment.
3.1 Customer shall pay the fees set out in each Order Form. The initial Order Form sets a monthly Services fee of $38,000.
3.2 Invoices are issued monthly in advance and are due within 45 days of the invoice date. Disputed amounts must be notified in writing within 15 days of the invoice date, and Customer shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.
3.3 Price Adjustments. Provider may increase fees once per contract year by no more than 4%, on at least 60 days' prior written notice.
3.4 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of sales, use and value-added taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

4. Data Protection and Security.
4.1 Provider shall maintain a written information security program and shall obtain an independent SOC 2 Type II report at least annually, a copy of which shall be provided to Customer on request.
4.2 Security Incidents. Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation.
4.3 Backups. Provider shall perform daily backups of Customer Data and retain each backup for 35 days. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 4 hours.
4.4 Data Location. Customer Data shall be stored only in data centres located in the Eastmarch region.

5. Term and Termination.
5.1 This MSA has an initial term of three (3) years from its effective date and renews for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
5.2 Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on 120 days' written notice, subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the fees remaining for the then-current term of that Order Form.
5.3 Either party may terminate this MSA if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure within 30 days of written notice.
5.4 Transition Assistance. On expiry or termination, Provider shall provide up to 60 days of transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates.

6. Liability.
6.1 Except for indemnification obligations and breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability under this MSA shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
6.2 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.
6.3 Chronic Failure. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage is below 99.0% in any three (3) months within a rolling six (6) month period, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without paying any early termination fee.

7. Governing Law. This MSA is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. — By: Anselm Vardaman, CEO
Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society — By: Gwendolyn Tarrow-Bligh, COO

question: Suppose the accepted market-entry model projects first-year revenue of $1,500,000. What success fee does Tessaline owe Brindlewick?
pages:
EXAMPLE CONSULTING AGREEMENT

This Consulting Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 10 June 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC, a limited liability company with offices at 19 Gantry Lane, Millhaven ("Consultant"), and Tessaline Outdoor Co., a corporation with offices at 640 Ridgeback Avenue, Cedar Hollow ("Company").

1. Definitions.
1.1 "Deliverables" means the reports, models and presentations described in Exhibit A.
1.2 "Project" means the market-entry assessment for the Company's proposed line of lightweight camping stoves.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Cedar Hollow.

2. Services. Consultant shall perform the Project and deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the timeline in Exhibit A. Consultant shall assign a lead consultant who will devote not less than 20 hours per week to the Project.

3. Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6) months (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter it renews automatically for successive three (3) month periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 15 Business Days before the end of the then-current term.

4. Minimum Commitment. The Company may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the first three (3) months of the Initial Term. After the third month, the Company may terminate for convenience on 20 Business Days' written notice.

5. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after receiving written notice of it.

6. Fees. The Company shall pay Consultant a monthly fee of $14,500 (the "Monthly Fee"). In addition, upon acceptance of the final Deliverable the Company shall pay a success fee equal to 4% of the first-year projected revenue stated in the accepted market-entry model, capped at $40,000.

7. Payment Terms. Consultant shall invoice the Monthly Fee on the first Business Day of each month. The Company shall pay each invoice within 30 days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month, and Consultant may suspend the Services if any invoice remains unpaid more than 45 days after receipt.

8. Expenses. The Company shall reimburse reasonable travel expenses pre-approved in writing. Airfare shall be economy class for flights under five (5) hours.

9. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of three (3) years after termination of this Agreement. This obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party.

10. Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees, all rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Company. Consultant retains ownership of its pre-existing methodologies, templates and tools, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the Deliverables.

11. Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who worked on the Project.

12. Insurance. Consultant shall maintain professional liability insurance with a limit of not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

13. Limitation of Liability. Except for breaches of Section 9, neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14. Governing Law and Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch. The courts located in Millhaven shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

15. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set out above.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC — By: Odalys Brindlewick, Principal
Tessaline Outdoor Co. — By: Marten Tessaline, President

question: Monthly uptime came in at 99.3%. What service credit is Hollowbrook owed on the initial $38,000 monthly fee?
pages:
MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
(Example — for testing purposes)

This Master Services Agreement ("MSA") is effective 15 January 2025 between Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. ("Provider") and Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society ("Customer").

1. Definitions.
"Services" means the managed hosting, monitoring and backup services described in each Order Form.
"Order Form" means an ordering document executed by both parties that references this MSA.
"Monthly Uptime Percentage" means the total minutes in a calendar month minus minutes of Downtime, divided by the total minutes in that month.
"Downtime" means any period of more than five (5) consecutive minutes during which the production environment is unreachable, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and performed between 01:00 and 05:00 local time, not exceeding eight (8) hours per month.

2. Service Levels.
2.1 Provider shall make the production environment available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%.
2.2 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.5%, Customer will receive a credit of 5% of the monthly Services fee; below 99.5% but at least 99.0%, a credit of 10%; and below 99.0%, a credit of 25%. Service Credits in any month shall not exceed 25% of that month's fees.
2.3 Claims. Customer must request Service Credits within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for failure to meet the service levels, except as provided in Section 6.3.
2.4 Support Response. Provider shall respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes, Severity 2 incidents within 2 hours, and Severity 3 incidents within 1 Business Day.

3. Fees and Payment.
3.1 Customer shall pay the fees set out in each Order Form. The initial Order Form sets a monthly Services fee of $38,000.
3.2 Invoices are issued monthly in advance and are due within 45 days of the invoice date. Disputed amounts must be notified in writing within 15 days of the invoice date, and Customer shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.
3.3 Price Adjustments. Provider may increase fees once per contract year by no more than 4%, on at least 60 days' prior written notice.
3.4 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of sales, use and value-added taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

4. Data Protection and Security.
4.1 Provider shall maintain a written information security program and shall obtain an independent SOC 2 Type II report at least annually, a copy of which shall be provided to Customer on request.
4.2 Security Incidents. Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation.
4.3 Backups. Provider shall perform daily backups of Customer Data and retain each backup for 35 days. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 4 hours.
4.4 Data Location. Customer Data shall be stored only in data centres located in the Eastmarch region.

5. Term and Termination.
5.1 This MSA has an initial term of three (3) years from its effective date and renews for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
5.2 Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on 120 days' written notice, subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the fees remaining for the then-current term of that Order Form.
5.3 Either party may terminate this MSA if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure within 30 days of written notice.
5.4 Transition Assistance. On expiry or termination, Provider shall provide up to 60 days of transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates.

6. Liability.
6.1 Except for indemnification obligations and breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability under this MSA shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
6.2 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.
6.3 Chronic Failure. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage is below 99.0% in any three (3) months within a rolling six (6) month period, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without paying any early termination fee.

7. Governing Law. This MSA is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. — By: Anselm Vardaman, CEO
Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society — By: Gwendolyn Tarrow-Bligh, COO

raw.answer: At 99.3% monthly uptime, Hollowbrook is entitled to a 10% service credit, which on the $38,000 monthly Services fee equals $3,800. Hollowbrook must request the credit within 30 days after the end of the affected month.

question: If Coralie pays rent on the 25th of the month, what's the late fee?

RESIDENTIAL TENANCY AGREEMENT — EXAMPLE

Landlord: Pemberton Ashgrove, 61 Orchard Vale, Wexbury
Tenant: Coralie Dunmore
Property: Apartment 3, 47 Larkspur Row, Wexbury (the "Property")
Agreement Date: 28 June 2025

1. Term. The tenancy begins on 1 July 2025 and ends on 30 June 2026 (the "Fixed Term"). After the Fixed Term, the tenancy continues month to month unless either party gives notice under Section 9.

2. Rent. The rent is $1,875 per month, due on the 1st day of each month. Rent may be paid by bank transfer or cheque.

3. Late Rent. Rent not received by the 5th day of the month incurs a late fee of $60, plus $8 for each additional day the rent remains unpaid, up to a maximum late fee of $150 per month.

4. Security Deposit. The Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $2,800 on or before the start of the tenancy. The Landlord shall return the deposit, less itemised deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, within 21 days after the Tenant vacates.

5. Utilities. The Tenant pays electricity, gas and internet. The Landlord pays water, sewer and refuse collection.

6. Pets. The Tenant may keep one (1) cat or one (1) dog under 25 pounds. A non-refundable pet fee of $300 is payable before the pet moves in, and pet rent of $35 per month applies.

7. Occupancy. The Property may be occupied by no more than two (2) adults and their dependent children.

8. Maintenance. The Tenant shall keep the Property clean and promptly report any needed repairs. The Landlord shall complete urgent repairs affecting heating, water or security within 48 hours of being notified and other repairs within a reasonable time.

9. Ending the Tenancy. During the Fixed Term, the Tenant may end the tenancy early only by paying an early termination fee equal to one month's rent and giving at least 30 days' written notice. During any month-to-month period, either party may end the tenancy by giving at least 60 days' written notice.

10. Entry. The Landlord may enter the Property for inspections or repairs after giving the Tenant at least 24 hours' notice, except in an emergency.

11. Smoking. Smoking of any substance is prohibited inside the Property and on its balcony.

12. Alterations. The Tenant shall not paint, install fixtures or make any alteration without the Landlord's written consent.

13. Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the entire agreement between the parties regarding the tenancy.

Signed by the Landlord: Pemberton Ashgrove
Signed by the Tenant: Coralie Dunmore

raw.answer: The late fee would be $150, the monthly maximum. Paying on the 25th is well past the 5th-day deadline, and the $60 base fee plus $8 per additional day exceeds the cap.
raw.explanation: Under Section 3 (Late Rent), rent not received by the 5th incurs a $60 fee plus $8 for each additional day it remains unpaid, capped at $150 per month. Rent is due on the 1st under Section 2. Whether you count about 19 or 20 additional days after the 5th, the total ($212 or $220) is above the cap, so the fee is limited to $150.
not_stated: Exactly how the 'additional days' are counted (for example, whether the day of payment is included). This does not change the result because the cap applies either way.

Each is a "Party" and, when disclosing, the "Discloser"; when receiving, the "Recipient".

1. Purpose. The Parties wish to evaluate a possible joint development of warehouse picking software (the "Purpose").

2. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Discloser, whether oral, written or electronic, that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Oral disclosures must be summarised in writing and marked confidential within 14 days of disclosure to be protected.

3. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public other than through breach of this NDA; (b) was known to the Recipient before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Confidential Information; or (d) is received from a third party without restriction.

4. Obligations. The Recipient shall (a) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations no less protective than this NDA; and (c) protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care.

5. Compelled Disclosure. If the Recipient is required by law to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the Discloser prompt notice, where legally permitted, so that the Discloser may seek a protective order.

6. Term. This NDA applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years following its date. The obligations in Section 4 survive for five (5) years after the last disclosure, except that obligations relating to source code survive indefinitely.

7. Return or Destruction. Within 30 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy all Confidential Information, and an officer of the Recipient shall certify destruction in writing within 10 days thereafter.

8. No Licence. Nothing in this NDA grants any licence under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right, except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

9. No Obligation. Neither Party is obliged to proceed with any transaction. Either Party may end discussions at any time by written notice.

10. Remedies. Each Party acknowledges that breach may cause irreparable harm and that the Discloser may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

11. Governing Law. This NDA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ostervale, and the courts of Dunmarrow have non-exclusive jurisdiction.

Signed for Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd.: Ines Fernwhistle, Director
Signed for Plumtree Analytica GmbH: Jurgen Pfeffer-Lind, Managing Director

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
(Example — for testing purposes)

This Master Services Agreement ("MSA") is effective 15 January 2025 between Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. ("Provider") and Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society ("Customer").

1. Definitions.
"Services" means the managed hosting, monitoring and backup services described in each Order Form.
"Order Form" means an ordering document executed by both parties that references this MSA.
"Monthly Uptime Percentage" means the total minutes in a calendar month minus minutes of Downtime, divided by the total minutes in that month.
"Downtime" means any period of more than five (5) consecutive minutes during which the production environment is unreachable, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and performed between 01:00 and 05:00 local time, not exceeding eight (8) hours per month.

2. Service Levels.
2.1 Provider shall make the production environment available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%.
2.2 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.5%, Customer will receive a credit of 5% of the monthly Services fee; below 99.5% but at least 99.0%, a credit of 10%; and below 99.0%, a credit of 25%. Service Credits in any month shall not exceed 25% of that month's fees.
2.3 Claims. Customer must request Service Credits within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for failure to meet the service levels, except as provided in Section 6.3.
2.4 Support Response. Provider shall respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes, Severity 2 incidents within 2 hours, and Severity 3 incidents within 1 Business Day.

3. Fees and Payment.
3.1 Customer shall pay the fees set out in each Order Form. The initial Order Form sets a monthly Services fee of $38,000.
3.2 Invoices are issued monthly in advance and are due within 45 days of the invoice date. Disputed amounts must be notified in writing within 15 days of the invoice date, and Customer shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.
3.3 Price Adjustments. Provider may increase fees once per contract year by no more than 4%, on at least 60 days' prior written notice.
3.4 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of sales, use and value-added taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

4. Data Protection and Security.
4.1 Provider shall maintain a written information security program and shall obtain an independent SOC 2 Type II report at least annually, a copy of which shall be provided to Customer on request.
4.2 Security Incidents. Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation.
4.3 Backups. Provider shall perform daily backups of Customer Data and retain each backup for 35 days. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 4 hours.
4.4 Data Location. Customer Data shall be stored only in data centres located in the Eastmarch region.

5. Term and Termination.
5.1 This MSA has an initial term of three (3) years from its effective date and renews for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
5.2 Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on 120 days' written notice, subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the fees remaining for the then-current term of that Order Form.
5.3 Either party may terminate this MSA if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure within 30 days of written notice.
5.4 Transition Assistance. On expiry or termination, Provider shall provide up to 60 days of transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates.

6. Liability.
6.1 Except for indemnification obligations and breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability under this MSA shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
6.2 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.
6.3 Chronic Failure. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage is below 99.0% in any three (3) months within a rolling six (6) month period, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without paying any early termination fee.

7. Governing Law. This MSA is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. — By: Anselm Vardaman, CEO
Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society — By: Gwendolyn Tarrow-Bligh, COO

question: Is there a cap on either party's liability in the Tamsin Rowe staffing agreement?
pages:
STAFFING SERVICES AGREEMENT

Dated 9 October 2025 between Tamsin Rowe Staffing Group Inc. ("Agency") and Northgale Freight Services LLC ("Client").

1. Services. Agency will supply temporary warehouse associates and forklift operators ("Associates") to Client's distribution centre at 2200 Ironwood Parkway, Millhaven.

2. Bill Rates. Client shall pay Agency the following hourly bill rates: warehouse associates, $27.40; certified forklift operators, $31.85. Overtime hours (over 40 per week) are billed at 1.5 times the applicable bill rate, and hours worked on Agency-recognized holidays are billed at 2 times the applicable bill rate.

3. Timesheets. Client shall approve Associates' timesheets electronically by 10:00 a.m. each Monday for the prior week. Unapproved timesheets are deemed approved after 48 hours.

4. Invoicing. Agency invoices weekly. Invoices are due within 15 days of the invoice date.

5. Conversion Fee. If Client hires an Associate directly within the first 520 hours worked by that Associate on assignment, Client shall pay a conversion fee equal to 20% of the Associate's first-year base salary. After 520 hours, no conversion fee applies.

6. Minimum Shift. Client shall pay for a minimum of four (4) hours for any Associate who reports for a scheduled shift and is sent home early.

7. Supervision. Client shall supervise Associates' day-to-day work and provide site-specific safety training before Associates begin work. Client shall not permit Associates to operate equipment for which they are not certified.

8. Workers' Compensation. Agency shall maintain workers' compensation insurance covering all Associates and shall provide a certificate of insurance on request.

9. Replacement. If Client is dissatisfied with an Associate for any lawful reason and notifies Agency within the first eight (8) hours of the assignment, Agency will not bill those hours and will provide a replacement.

10. Term. This Agreement continues until terminated by either party on 14 days' written notice.

11. Non-Solicitation of Agency Staff. Client shall not solicit Agency's internal recruiting employees for 12 months after termination.

12. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch.

Tamsin Rowe Staffing Group Inc. — By: Tamsin Rowe, President
Northgale Freight Services LLC — By: Idris Mallory-Quent, Director of Operations

raw.answer: No. The agreement does not contain any limitation or cap on either party's liability. It does not address liability limits at all.
raw.explanation: The agreement covers services, bill rates, timesheets, invoicing, conversion fees, minimum shifts, supervision, workers' compensation, replacement, term, non-solicitation and governing law, but none of these clauses limits or caps liability. The nearest related term is Section 8, which only requires Agency to maintain workers' compensation insurance.
not_stated: Any monetary cap on either party's liability
Any exclusion of indirect or consequential damages
Any indemnification obligations

question: If Carrowmore cancels partway through a year, does the Lumenbridge agreement give it a refund of prepaid fees?
pages:
SAAS SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

This SaaS Subscription Agreement (the "Agreement") is made effective 1 February 2026 between Lumenbridge Software Ltd. ("Lumenbridge") and Carrowmore Dental Group PLLC ("Subscriber").

1. Subscription. Lumenbridge grants Subscriber a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to access and use the Lumenbridge Chairside practice-management platform (the "Platform") during the Subscription Term for Subscriber's internal business purposes.

2. Users and Locations. The subscription covers up to 45 named users across 3 clinic locations. Additional named users are charged at $38 per user per month, and each additional clinic location is charged at $410 per month.

3. Fees. The base subscription fee is $4,960 per month, billed annually in advance at $59,520 per year. A one-time implementation fee of $7,500 is payable on signature.

4. Payment. Invoices are due net 30. Lumenbridge may suspend access if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid 15 days after written notice of non-payment.

5. Subscription Term and Renewal. The initial Subscription Term is 24 months. Thereafter the Agreement renews automatically for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of the current term. Renewal pricing may increase by no more than 7% over the prior term's fees.

6. Service Availability. Lumenbridge will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available 99.5% of the time each month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least 48 hours in advance.

7. Support. Standard support is available by email and phone from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. Critical issues reported by phone will receive a response within 1 hour during support hours.

8. Data Ownership. As between the parties, Subscriber owns all patient and practice data entered into the Platform ("Subscriber Data"). Lumenbridge may use aggregated, de-identified data to improve the Platform.

9. Data Export and Deletion. Upon termination, Subscriber may export Subscriber Data in CSV format for 30 days. After that period, Lumenbridge will delete Subscriber Data within 90 days, except as required by law.

10. Health Information. The parties shall enter into a Business Associate Agreement in the form of Exhibit C, which governs Lumenbridge's handling of protected health information.

11. Breach Notification. Lumenbridge will notify Subscriber of any unauthorized access to Subscriber Data within 72 hours of discovery.

12. Limitation of Liability. Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid by Subscriber in the 12 months preceding the claim, except that the cap for breaches of Section 10 or Section 11 is two times (2x) that amount.

13. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate on 30 days' written notice of a material breach that remains uncured at the end of that period.

14. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Lumenbridge Software Ltd. — By: Aurelio Fenwick-Strand, Chief Revenue Officer
Carrowmore Dental Group PLLC — By: Dr. Niamh Carrowmore, Managing Dentist

raw.answer: The agreement does not address refunds of prepaid fees, so it does not provide one if Carrowmore cancels mid-year. It also contains no right to cancel for convenience partway through a term; the only exits it describes are non-renewal at the end of a term and termination for an uncured material breach.
raw.explanation: Section 3 bills the base fee annually in advance, but no clause says what happens to prepaid amounts on early termination. Section 5 allows ending the agreement only by written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of the current term. Section 13 allows termination on 30 days' written notice of an uncured material breach.

question: If Plumtree gets a subpoena for Fernwhistle's information, how many days' notice does it have to give Fernwhistle?
pages:
MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (TEST DOCUMENT)

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the "NDA") is made on 2 September 2025 between Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd., registered office 7 Copperleaf Yard, Dunmarrow ("Fernwhistle"), and Plumtree Analytica GmbH, Kastanienweg 21, Ostervale ("Plumtree"). Each is a "Party" and, when disclosing, the "Discloser"; when receiving, the "Recipient".

1. Purpose. The Parties wish to evaluate a possible joint development of warehouse picking software (the "Purpose").

2. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Discloser, whether oral, written or electronic, that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Oral disclosures must be summarised in writing and marked confidential within 14 days of disclosure to be protected.

3. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public other than through breach of this NDA; (b) was known to the Recipient before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Confidential Information; or (d) is received from a third party without restriction.

4. Obligations. The Recipient shall (a) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations no less protective than this NDA; and (c) protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care.

5. Compelled Disclosure. If the Recipient is required by law to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the Discloser prompt notice, where legally permitted, so that the Discloser may seek a protective order.

6. Term. This NDA applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years following its date. The obligations in Section 4 survive for five (5) years after the last disclosure, except that obligations relating to source code survive indefinitely.

7. Return or Destruction. Within 30 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy all Confidential Information, and an officer of the Recipient shall certify destruction in writing within 10 days thereafter.

8. No Licence. Nothing in this NDA grants any licence under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right, except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

9. No Obligation. Neither Party is obliged to proceed with any transaction. Either Party may end discussions at any time by written notice.

10. Remedies. Each Party acknowledges that breach may cause irreparable harm and that the Discloser may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

11. Governing Law. This NDA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ostervale, and the courts of Dunmarrow have non-exclusive jurisdiction.

Signed for Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd.: Ines Fernwhistle, Director
Signed for Plumtree Analytica GmbH: Jurgen Pfeffer-Lind, Managing Director

raw.answer: The NDA does not set a specific number of days. Under Section 5 (Compelled Disclosure), Plumtree must give Fernwhistle "prompt notice, where legally permitted," so that Fernwhistle can seek a protective order.
raw.explanation: When Plumtree receives Fernwhistle's information, it is the Recipient and Fernwhistle is the Discloser. Section 5 applies when the Recipient is required by law to disclose Confidential Information. It requires prompt notice without fixing a deadline in days, and only where the law allows notice to be given.

EXAMPLE CONSULTING AGREEMENT

This Consulting Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 10 June 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC, a limited liability company with offices at 19 Gantry Lane, Millhaven ("Consultant"), and Tessaline Outdoor Co., a corporation with offices at 640 Ridgeback Avenue, Cedar Hollow ("Company").

1. Definitions.
1.1 "Deliverables" means the reports, models and presentations described in Exhibit A.
1.2 "Project" means the market-entry assessment for the Company's proposed line of lightweight camping stoves.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Cedar Hollow.

2. Services. Consultant shall perform the Project and deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the timeline in Exhibit A. Consultant shall assign a lead consultant who will devote not less than 20 hours per week to the Project.

3. Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6) months (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter it renews automatically for successive three (3) month periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 15 Business Days before the end of the then-current term.

4. Minimum Commitment. The Company may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the first three (3) months of the Initial Term. After the third month, the Company may terminate for convenience on 20 Business Days' written notice.

5. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after receiving written notice of it.

6. Fees. The Company shall pay Consultant a monthly fee of $14,500 (the "Monthly Fee"). In addition, upon acceptance of the final Deliverable the Company shall pay a success fee equal to 4% of the first-year projected revenue stated in the accepted market-entry model, capped at $40,000.

7. Payment Terms. Consultant shall invoice the Monthly Fee on the first Business Day of each month. The Company shall pay each invoice within 30 days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month, and Consultant may suspend the Services if any invoice remains unpaid more than 45 days after receipt.

8. Expenses. The Company shall reimburse reasonable travel expenses pre-approved in writing. Airfare shall be economy class for flights under five (5) hours.

9. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of three (3) years after termination of this Agreement. This obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party.

10. Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees, all rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Company. Consultant retains ownership of its pre-existing methodologies, templates and tools, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the Deliverables.

11. Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who worked on the Project.

12. Insurance. Consultant shall maintain professional liability insurance with a limit of not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

13. Limitation of Liability. Except for breaches of Section 9, neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14. Governing Law and Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch. The courts located in Millhaven shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

15. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set out above.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC — By: Odalys Brindlewick, Principal
Tessaline Outdoor Co. — By: Marten Tessaline, President

question: How long do I have to dispute a bill from the firm?
pages:
ENGAGEMENT LETTER — LEGAL SERVICES
Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP
Attorneys at Law, 300 Harbourmaster Plaza, Wexbury

12 August 2025

Mr. Danforth Ilsley
27 Thistlecombe Road, Wexbury

Re: Representation in Ilsley v. Corvane Home Builders (the "Matter")

Dear Mr. Ilsley:

Thank you for selecting Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP (the "Firm") to represent you. This letter sets out the scope and terms of our engagement.

1. Scope. The Firm will represent you in the Matter, which concerns alleged construction defects at your residence, through the conclusion of proceedings in the Wexbury County Court. The engagement does not include any appeal, any claim against your insurer, or any related property tax matters, each of which would require a separate engagement letter.

2. Staffing. Partner Lucinda Castellane will have primary responsibility for the Matter. She may be assisted by associates and paralegals as she considers appropriate.

3. Hourly Rates. Fees are based on time spent, recorded in increments of one-tenth (0.1) of an hour. Current hourly rates are: partners, $610; associates, $395; and paralegals, $175. Rates are reviewed each January and may increase by up to 6% per year.

4. Advance Fee Deposit. Before work begins, you will deposit $15,000 into the Firm's client trust account. The Firm will draw on the deposit to pay each invoice and may ask you to replenish it to $15,000 whenever the balance falls below $5,000. Any unused portion of the deposit will be refunded at the end of the engagement.

5. Costs. You will reimburse court filing fees, expert witness fees, deposition transcript costs and courier charges at actual cost. The Firm will not incur any single cost exceeding $2,500 without your prior approval.

6. Billing. The Firm will send itemized invoices monthly. Payment is due upon receipt. If you have a question about an invoice, please raise it with Ms. Castellane within a reasonable time so that it can be resolved.

7. Settlement Authority. The Firm will not settle the Matter without your express authorization. The Firm will promptly communicate all settlement offers to you.

8. Termination of Representation. You may terminate the Firm's representation at any time by written notice. The Firm may withdraw for good cause, including non-payment, subject to court approval where required. Fees and costs incurred before termination remain payable.

9. File Retention. After the Matter closes, the Firm will retain your file for five (5) years. You may request your file at any time before then.

10. No Guarantee. The Firm cannot guarantee any particular outcome. Any statements about possible results are opinions only.

11. Fee Disputes. Any dispute regarding the Firm's fees shall first be submitted to the Wexbury Bar Association fee mediation program before either party commences litigation.

12. Conflicts. The Firm has run a conflicts check and has found no conflicts of interest relating to Corvane Home Builders or its principals.

If these terms are acceptable, please sign below and return this letter together with the advance fee deposit.

Very truly yours,
Lucinda Castellane, Partner, for Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP

AGREED: ____________________ Danforth Ilsley   Date: 15 August 2025

raw.answer: The agreement sets no specific deadline for disputing a bill. Under Billing (clause 6), you should raise any question about an invoice with Ms. Castellane "within a reasonable time," and any fee dispute must first go to the Wexbury Bar Association fee mediation program before either side sues (clause 11).
raw.explanation: Clause 6 asks you to raise invoice questions within a reasonable time but does not define that period in days. Clause 11 sets out the process for a fee dispute, mediation before litigation, but gives no time limit for starting it. Payment itself is due upon receipt.

1. Term. The tenancy begins on 1 July 2025 and ends on 30 June 2026 (the "Fixed Term"). After the Fixed Term, the tenancy continues month to month unless either party gives notice under Section 9.

2. Rent. The rent is $1,875 per month, due on the 1st day of each month. Rent may be paid by bank transfer or cheque.

3. Late Rent. Rent not received by the 5th day of the month incurs a late fee of $60, plus $8 for each additional day the rent remains unpaid, up to a maximum late fee of $150 per month.

4. Security Deposit. The Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $2,800 on or before the start of the tenancy. The Landlord shall return the deposit, less itemised deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear, within 21 days after the Tenant vacates.

5. Utilities. The Tenant pays electricity, gas and internet. The Landlord pays water, sewer and refuse collection.

6. Pets. The Tenant may keep one (1) cat or one (1) dog under 25 pounds. A non-refundable pet fee of $300 is payable before the pet moves in, and pet rent of $35 per month applies.

7. Occupancy. The Property may be occupied by no more than two (2) adults and their dependent children.

8. Maintenance. The Tenant shall keep the Property clean and promptly report any needed repairs. The Landlord shall complete urgent repairs affecting heating, water or security within 48 hours of being notified and other repairs within a reasonable time.

This Master Services Agreement ("MSA") is effective 15 January 2025 between Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. ("Provider") and Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society ("Customer").

1. Definitions.
"Services" means the managed hosting, monitoring and backup services described in each Order Form.
"Order Form" means an ordering document executed by both parties that references this MSA.
"Monthly Uptime Percentage" means the total minutes in a calendar month minus minutes of Downtime, divided by the total minutes in that month.
"Downtime" means any period of more than five (5) consecutive minutes during which the production environment is unreachable, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and performed between 01:00 and 05:00 local time, not exceeding eight (8) hours per month.

2. Service Levels.
2.1 Provider shall make the production environment available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%.
2.2 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.5%, Customer will receive a credit of 5% of the monthly Services fee; below 99.5% but at least 99.0%, a credit of 10%; and below 99.0%, a credit of 25%. Service Credits in any month shall not exceed 25% of that month's fees.
2.3 Claims. Customer must request Service Credits within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for failure to meet the service levels, except as provided in Section 6.3.
2.4 Support Response. Provider shall respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes, Severity 2 incidents within 2 hours, and Severity 3 incidents within 1 Business Day.

3. Fees and Payment.
3.1 Customer shall pay the fees set out in each Order Form. The initial Order Form sets a monthly Services fee of $38,000.
3.2 Invoices are issued monthly in advance and are due within 45 days of the invoice date. Disputed amounts must be notified in writing within 15 days of the invoice date, and Customer shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.
3.3 Price Adjustments. Provider may increase fees once per contract year by no more than 4%, on at least 60 days' prior written notice.
3.4 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of sales, use and value-added taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

4. Data Protection and Security.
4.1 Provider shall maintain a written information security program and shall obtain an independent SOC 2 Type II report at least annually, a copy of which shall be provided to Customer on request.
4.2 Security Incidents. Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation.
4.3 Backups. Provider shall perform daily backups of Customer Data and retain each backup for 35 days. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 4 hours.
4.4 Data Location. Customer Data shall be stored only in data centres located in the Eastmarch region.

5. Term and Termination.
5.1 This MSA has an initial term of three (3) years from its effective date and renews for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
5.2 Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on 120 days' written notice, subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the fees remaining for the then-current term of that Order Form.
5.3 Either party may terminate this MSA if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure within 30 days of written notice.
5.4 Transition Assistance. On expiry or termination, Provider shall provide up to 60 days of transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates.

6. Liability.
6.1 Except for indemnification obligations and breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability under this MSA shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
6.2 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.
6.3 Chronic Failure. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage is below 99.0% in any three (3) months within a rolling six (6) month period, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without paying any early termination fee.

7. Governing Law. This MSA is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. — By: Anselm Vardaman, CEO
Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society — By: Gwendolyn Tarrow-Bligh, COO

1. Definitions.
1.1 "Deliverables" means the reports, models and presentations described in Exhibit A.
1.2 "Project" means the market-entry assessment for the Company's proposed line of lightweight camping stoves.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Cedar Hollow.

2. Services. Consultant shall perform the Project and deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the timeline in Exhibit A. Consultant shall assign a lead consultant who will devote not less than 20 hours per week to the Project.

3. Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6) months (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter it renews automatically for successive three (3) month periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 15 Business Days before the end of the then-current term.

4. Minimum Commitment. The Company may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the first three (3) months of the Initial Term. After the third month, the Company may terminate for convenience on 20 Business Days' written notice.

5. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after receiving written notice of it.

6. Fees. The Company shall pay Consultant a monthly fee of $14,500 (the "Monthly Fee"). In addition, upon acceptance of the final Deliverable the Company shall pay a success fee equal to 4% of the first-year projected revenue stated in the accepted market-entry model, capped at $40,000.

7. Payment Terms. Consultant shall invoice the Monthly Fee on the first Business Day of each month. The Company shall pay each invoice within 30 days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month, and Consultant may suspend the Services if any invoice remains unpaid more than 45 days after receipt.

8. Expenses. The Company shall reimburse reasonable travel expenses pre-approved in writing. Airfare shall be economy class for flights under five (5) hours.

9. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of three (3) years after termination of this Agreement. This obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party.

10. Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees, all rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Company. Consultant retains ownership of its pre-existing methodologies, templates and tools, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the Deliverables.

11. Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who worked on the Project.

12. Insurance. Consultant shall maintain professional liability insurance with a limit of not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

13. Limitation of Liability. Except for breaches of Section 9, neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14. Governing Law and Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch. The courts located in Millhaven shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

15. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set out above.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC — By: Odalys Brindlewick, Principal
Tessaline Outdoor Co. — By: Marten Tessaline, President

MUTUAL NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (TEST DOCUMENT)

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (the "NDA") is made on 2 September 2025 between Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd., registered office 7 Copperleaf Yard, Dunmarrow ("Fernwhistle"), and Plumtree Analytica GmbH, Kastanienweg 21, Ostervale ("Plumtree"). Each is a "Party" and, when disclosing, the "Discloser"; when receiving, the "Recipient".

1. Purpose. The Parties wish to evaluate a possible joint development of warehouse picking software (the "Purpose").

2. Confidential Information. "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Discloser, whether oral, written or electronic, that is marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Oral disclosures must be summarised in writing and marked confidential within 14 days of disclosure to be protected.

3. Exclusions. Confidential Information does not include information that (a) is or becomes public other than through breach of this NDA; (b) was known to the Recipient before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Confidential Information; or (d) is received from a third party without restriction.

4. Obligations. The Recipient shall (a) use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; (b) disclose it only to its employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by obligations no less protective than this NDA; and (c) protect it using at least the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, and no less than reasonable care.

5. Compelled Disclosure. If the Recipient is required by law to disclose Confidential Information, it shall give the Discloser prompt notice, where legally permitted, so that the Discloser may seek a protective order.

6. Term. This NDA applies to disclosures made during the two (2) years following its date. The obligations in Section 4 survive for five (5) years after the last disclosure, except that obligations relating to source code survive indefinitely.

7. Return or Destruction. Within 30 days after a written request, the Recipient shall return or destroy all Confidential Information, and an officer of the Recipient shall certify destruction in writing within 10 days thereafter.

8. No Licence. Nothing in this NDA grants any licence under any patent, copyright or other intellectual property right, except the limited right to use Confidential Information for the Purpose.

9. No Obligation. Neither Party is obliged to proceed with any transaction. Either Party may end discussions at any time by written notice.

10. Remedies. Each Party acknowledges that breach may cause irreparable harm and that the Discloser may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy.

11. Governing Law. This NDA is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ostervale, and the courts of Dunmarrow have non-exclusive jurisdiction.

Signed for Fernwhistle Robotics Ltd.: Ines Fernwhistle, Director
Signed for Plumtree Analytica GmbH: Jurgen Pfeffer-Lind, Managing Director

Section 6 also says the NDA covers only disclosures made during the two years following its date of 2 September 2025.

1.1 Premises: Unit 4B, 112 Fennimore Street, Port Avalon, comprising approximately 1,850 rentable square feet (the "Premises").
1.2 Term: Five (5) years, commencing 1 May 2025 (the "Commencement Date") and ending 30 April 2030.
1.3 Base Rent: $5,550 per month for Lease Years 1 and 2; $5,790 per month for Lease Years 3 and 4; and $6,020 per month for Lease Year 5.
1.4 Security Deposit: $11,100.
1.5 Permitted Use: operation of a café serving food and non-alcoholic beverages for on-site and take-away consumption.

ARTICLE 2 — RENT
2.1 Payment. Base Rent is payable in advance on the first day of each calendar month without demand, deduction or set-off.
2.2 Late Charge. If any installment of Base Rent is not received within five (5) days after its due date, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to 5% of the overdue amount. Any amount remaining unpaid for more than 30 days shall also bear interest at 10% per annum.
2.3 Rent Abatement. Provided Tenant is not in default, Base Rent for the first two (2) full calendar months of the Term shall be abated.
2.4 Operating Expenses. In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay its Proportionate Share of Operating Expenses, which is 12.4%. Landlord shall provide an annual reconciliation statement within 120 days after the end of each calendar year.

ARTICLE 3 — SECURITY DEPOSIT
3.1 Landlord shall hold the Security Deposit as security for Tenant's performance. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to cure any default, and Tenant shall restore the amount so applied within ten (10) days after written demand.
3.2 Return. Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, less any lawful deductions, within 45 days after the expiration of the Term and Tenant's surrender of the Premises.

ARTICLE 4 — USE AND COMPLIANCE
4.1 Tenant shall use the Premises only for the Permitted Use and shall comply with all applicable laws.
4.2 Operating Hours. Tenant shall keep the Premises open to the public at least six (6) days per week.
4.3 Signage. Tenant may install exterior signage at its own cost, subject to Landlord's prior written approval of the design.

ARTICLE 5 — MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS
5.1 Landlord shall maintain the roof, foundation, structural walls and the building's main electrical and plumbing lines up to the point of entry into the Premises.
5.2 Tenant shall maintain the interior of the Premises, including fixtures, kitchen equipment and the dedicated HVAC unit serving the Premises, and shall keep a service contract for the HVAC unit with a licensed contractor.
5.3 Alterations. Tenant shall not make alterations costing more than $7,500 in the aggregate without Landlord's prior written consent.

ARTICLE 6 — INSURANCE
6.1 Tenant shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 in the aggregate, naming Landlord as additional insured.

ARTICLE 7 — ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING
7.1 Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet any part of the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold.

ARTICLE 8 — RENEWAL OPTION
8.1 Tenant has one (1) option to renew the Term for an additional five (5) years, exercisable by written notice delivered not less than 180 days and not more than 365 days before the expiration of the Term. Base Rent for the renewal term shall be the then-prevailing market rent, but not less than the Base Rent in effect during the final Lease Year.

ARTICLE 9 — DEFAULT
9.1 It is an Event of Default if Tenant fails to pay rent within ten (10) days after written notice of non-payment, or fails to cure any other breach within thirty (30) days after written notice.

ARTICLE 10 — EARLY TERMINATION
10.1 Tenant may terminate this Lease effective on the last day of Lease Year 3 by giving Landlord at least nine (9) months' prior written notice and paying a termination fee equal to three (3) months of the Base Rent then in effect.

ARTICLE 11 — MISCELLANEOUS
11.1 This Lease is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.
11.2 Notices shall be sent by certified mail or recognized overnight courier to the addresses on the signature page.

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement ("MSA") is effective 15 January 2025 between Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. ("Provider") and Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society ("Customer").

1. Definitions.
"Services" means the managed hosting, monitoring and backup services described in each Order Form.
"Order Form" means an ordering document executed by both parties that references this MSA.
"Monthly Uptime Percentage" means the total minutes in a calendar month minus minutes of Downtime, divided by the total minutes in that month.
"Downtime" means any period of more than five (5) consecutive minutes during which the production environment is unreachable, excluding Scheduled Maintenance.
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance notified to Customer at least 72 hours in advance and performed between 01:00 and 05:00 local time, not exceeding eight (8) hours per month.

2. Service Levels.
2.1 Provider shall make the production environment available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage of at least 99.9%.
2.2 Service Credits. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage falls below 99.9% but is at least 99.5%, Customer will receive a credit of 5% of the monthly Services fee; below 99.5% but at least 99.0%, a credit of 10%; and below 99.0%, a credit of 25%. Service Credits in any month shall not exceed 25% of that month's fees.
2.3 Claims. Customer must request Service Credits within 30 days after the end of the affected month. Service Credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for failure to meet the service levels, except as provided in Section 6.3.
2.4 Support Response. Provider shall respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes, Severity 2 incidents within 2 hours, and Severity 3 incidents within 1 Business Day.

3. Fees and Payment.
3.1 Customer shall pay the fees set out in each Order Form. The initial Order Form sets a monthly Services fee of $38,000.
3.2 Invoices are issued monthly in advance and are due within 45 days of the invoice date. Disputed amounts must be notified in writing within 15 days of the invoice date, and Customer shall pay the undisputed portion by the due date.
3.3 Price Adjustments. Provider may increase fees once per contract year by no more than 4%, on at least 60 days' prior written notice.
3.4 Taxes. Fees are exclusive of sales, use and value-added taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

4. Data Protection and Security.
4.1 Provider shall maintain a written information security program and shall obtain an independent SOC 2 Type II report at least annually, a copy of which shall be provided to Customer on request.
4.2 Security Incidents. Provider shall notify Customer of any confirmed Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours of confirmation.
4.3 Backups. Provider shall perform daily backups of Customer Data and retain each backup for 35 days. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 4 hours.
4.4 Data Location. Customer Data shall be stored only in data centres located in the Eastmarch region.

5. Term and Termination.
5.1 This MSA has an initial term of three (3) years from its effective date and renews for successive one (1) year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.
5.2 Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience on 120 days' written notice, subject to payment of an early termination fee equal to 50% of the fees remaining for the then-current term of that Order Form.
5.3 Either party may terminate this MSA if the other party materially breaches it and does not cure within 30 days of written notice.
5.4 Transition Assistance. On expiry or termination, Provider shall provide up to 60 days of transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates.

6. Liability.
6.1 Except for indemnification obligations and breaches of Section 4, each party's aggregate liability under this MSA shall not exceed the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
6.2 Neither party is liable for indirect, consequential or punitive damages.
6.3 Chronic Failure. If the Monthly Uptime Percentage is below 99.0% in any three (3) months within a rolling six (6) month period, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without paying any early termination fee.

7. Governing Law. This MSA is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Zephyrine Cloud Ops Inc. — By: Anselm Vardaman, CEO
Hollowbrook Mutual Assurance Society — By: Gwendolyn Tarrow-Bligh, COO

ENGAGEMENT LETTER — LEGAL SERVICES
Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP
Attorneys at Law, 300 Harbourmaster Plaza, Wexbury

12 August 2025

Mr. Danforth Ilsley
27 Thistlecombe Road, Wexbury

Re: Representation in Ilsley v. Corvane Home Builders (the "Matter")

Dear Mr. Ilsley:

Thank you for selecting Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP (the "Firm") to represent you. This letter sets out the scope and terms of our engagement.

1. Scope. The Firm will represent you in the Matter, which concerns alleged construction defects at your residence, through the conclusion of proceedings in the Wexbury County Court. The engagement does not include any appeal, any claim against your insurer, or any related property tax matters, each of which would require a separate engagement letter.

2. Staffing. Partner Lucinda Castellane will have primary responsibility for the Matter. She may be assisted by associates and paralegals as she considers appropriate.

3. Hourly Rates. Fees are based on time spent, recorded in increments of one-tenth (0.1) of an hour. Current hourly rates are: partners, $610; associates, $395; and paralegals, $175. Rates are reviewed each January and may increase by up to 6% per year.

4. Advance Fee Deposit. Before work begins, you will deposit $15,000 into the Firm's client trust account. The Firm will draw on the deposit to pay each invoice and may ask you to replenish it to $15,000 whenever the balance falls below $5,000. Any unused portion of the deposit will be refunded at the end of the engagement.

5. Costs. You will reimburse court filing fees, expert witness fees, deposition transcript costs and courier charges at actual cost. The Firm will not incur any single cost exceeding $2,500 without your prior approval.

6. Billing. The Firm will send itemized invoices monthly. Payment is due upon receipt. If you have a question about an invoice, please raise it with Ms. Castellane within a reasonable time so that it can be resolved.

7. Settlement Authority. The Firm will not settle the Matter without your express authorization. The Firm will promptly communicate all settlement offers to you.

8. Termination of Representation. You may terminate the Firm's representation at any time by written notice. The Firm may withdraw for good cause, including non-payment, subject to court approval where required. Fees and costs incurred before termination remain payable.

9. File Retention. After the Matter closes, the Firm will retain your file for five (5) years. You may request your file at any time before then.

10. No Guarantee. The Firm cannot guarantee any particular outcome. Any statements about possible results are opinions only.

11. Fee Disputes. Any dispute regarding the Firm's fees shall first be submitted to the Wexbury Bar Association fee mediation program before either party commences litigation.

12. Conflicts. The Firm has run a conflicts check and has found no conflicts of interest relating to Corvane Home Builders or its principals.

If these terms are acceptable, please sign below and return this letter together with the advance fee deposit.

Very truly yours,
Lucinda Castellane, Partner, for Castellane Rook & Pemberly LLP

AGREED: ____________________ Danforth Ilsley   Date: 15 August 2025
