INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR AGREEMENT (SAMPLE)

Between: Juniper Kestrel Media Ltd., 5 Saltmarsh Wharf, Brackenford (the "Company")
And: Rosalind Achterberg, sole trader, trading as Achterberg Edit, 14 Lindenfold Close, Brackenford (the "Contractor")
Date: 20 January 2026

1. Engagement. The Company engages the Contractor to provide video editing and colour grading services for the Company's documentary series "Tidelines" (the "Services").

2. Fees. The Company shall pay the Contractor a day rate of £520 for each full working day and £290 for each half day. Overtime beyond ten (10) hours in a single day is paid at £70 per hour.

3. Invoices. The Contractor shall invoice the Company fortnightly. The Company shall pay correctly submitted invoices within 14 days of receipt.

4. Independent Status. The Contractor is an independent contractor and not an employee. The Contractor is responsible for her own tax and national insurance contributions and shall indemnify the Company against any liability arising from her failure to pay them.

5. Equipment. The Contractor will provide her own editing workstation and software licences. The Company will provide access to its media server and a calibrated grading monitor at its premises when required.

6. Term and Termination. This Agreement starts on 2 February 2026 and continues until 31 July 2026 unless ended earlier. Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving seven (7) days' written notice. The Company may terminate immediately if the Contractor commits gross misconduct.

7. Intellectual Property. All rights in the edited footage, project files and grades created under this Agreement are assigned to the Company on creation.

8. Confidentiality. The Contractor shall not disclose any unreleased footage, scripts or broadcast schedules of the Company, whether during or after the term of this Agreement.

9. Credit. The Contractor shall receive an on-screen credit as "Editor" on each episode to which she contributes more than 50% of the editing days.

10. Substitution. The Contractor may send a suitably skilled substitute with the Company's prior approval, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld. The Contractor remains responsible for paying the substitute.

11. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the law of the Kingdom of Albermarch.

Signed: Odile Kestrel, Head of Post-Production, for Juniper Kestrel Media Ltd.
Signed: Rosalind Achterberg

raw.answer: The half-day rate is £290 for each half day (compared with £520 for each full working day).

This Software Development Agreement (the "Agreement") is made on 17 April 2025 between Mossgiel Labs Inc., 900 Foundry Row, Cedar Hollow ("Developer"), and Starling Quay Logistics Corp., 3 Pier Nine Road, Port Avalon ("Client").

1. Definitions.
"Application" means the route-planning web and mobile application described in the Specification.
"Specification" means the functional specification attached as Schedule 1.
"Milestone" means each stage of work listed in Section 3.
"Acceptance Tests" means the tests described in Schedule 2.

4. Acceptance. Client shall run the Acceptance Tests within ten (10) Business Days after delivery of each build and notify Developer in writing of any failures. Developer shall correct reported failures within fifteen (15) Business Days. If Client does not report failures within the ten (10) Business Day period, the build is deemed accepted.

pages:
EQUIPMENT RENTAL AGREEMENT (TEST)

Rental Agreement No. HLR-88213
Owner: Halvorsen Lift & Rig Rentals Co. ("Owner")
Renter: Oxbow Ridge Builders LLC ("Renter")
Jobsite: Lot 14, Kingsfoil Business Park, Brackenford

1. Equipment. Owner rents to Renter one (1) 60-foot articulating boom lift, serial no. AB60-4471, and one (1) 10,000-pound telehandler, serial no. TH10-0932 (together, the "Equipment").

2. Rental Rates. The boom lift rents at $480 per day, $1,650 per week or $4,300 per four-week period. The telehandler rents at $560 per day, $1,980 per week or $5,100 per four-week period. Rental periods begin when the Equipment leaves Owner's yard.

3. Delivery. Delivery and pickup are charged at $225 each way per machine.

4. Usage Limits. Rates are based on a single shift of up to 8 engine hours per day, 40 per week or 160 per four-week period. Hours in excess are charged at $45 per engine hour.

5. Damage Waiver. Renter may elect a damage waiver for 12% of the rental charges, which limits Renter's responsibility for accidental damage to $2,500 per occurrence. Without the waiver, Renter is responsible for the full cost of repair or replacement.

6. Fuel. Equipment is delivered full. If returned with less than a full tank, refuelling is charged at $6.75 per gallon.

7. Return. Renter shall return the Equipment clean and in the same condition as delivered, normal wear excepted. Renter must call Owner to schedule pickup at least 24 hours before the end of the rental period; rent continues to accrue until Owner is notified.

8. Operators. Only trained and certified operators employed by Renter may operate the Equipment.

9. Indemnity. Renter shall indemnify Owner against claims arising from Renter's use of the Equipment, except to the extent caused by Owner's negligence.

Owner: Halvorsen Lift & Rig Rentals Co. — By: Brynja Halvorsen
Renter: Oxbow Ridge Builders LLC — By: Callum Fairweather-Oxley

SAAS SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

This SaaS Subscription Agreement (the "Agreement") is made effective 1 February 2026 between Lumenbridge Software Ltd. ("Lumenbridge") and Carrowmore Dental Group PLLC ("Subscriber").

1. Subscription. Lumenbridge grants Subscriber a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to access and use the Lumenbridge Chairside practice-management platform (the "Platform") during the Subscription Term for Subscriber's internal business purposes.

2. Users and Locations. The subscription covers up to 45 named users across 3 clinic locations. Additional named users are charged at $38 per user per month, and each additional clinic location is charged at $410 per month.

3. Fees. The base subscription fee is $4,960 per month, billed annually in advance at $59,520 per year. A one-time implementation fee of $7,500 is payable on signature.

4. Payment. Invoices are due net 30. Lumenbridge may suspend access if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid 15 days after written notice of non-payment.

5. Subscription Term and Renewal. The initial Subscription Term is 24 months. Thereafter the Agreement renews automatically for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before the end of the current term. Renewal pricing may increase by no more than 7% over the prior term's fees.

6. Service Availability. Lumenbridge will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available 99.5% of the time each month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least 48 hours in advance.

7. Support. Standard support is available by email and phone from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. Critical issues reported by phone will receive a response within 1 hour during support hours.

8. Data Ownership. As between the parties, Subscriber owns all patient and practice data entered into the Platform ("Subscriber Data"). Lumenbridge may use aggregated, de-identified data to improve the Platform.

9. Data Export and Deletion. Upon termination, Subscriber may export Subscriber Data in CSV format for 30 days. After that period, Lumenbridge will delete Subscriber Data within 90 days, except as required by law.

10. Health Information. The parties shall enter into a Business Associate Agreement in the form of Exhibit C, which governs Lumenbridge's handling of protected health information.

11. Breach Notification. Lumenbridge will notify Subscriber of any unauthorized access to Subscriber Data within 72 hours of discovery.

12. Limitation of Liability. Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid by Subscriber in the 12 months preceding the claim, except that the cap for breaches of Section 10 or Section 11 is two times (2x) that amount.

13. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate on 30 days' written notice of a material breach that remains uncured at the end of that period.

14. Governing Law. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.

Lumenbridge Software Ltd. — By: Aurelio Fenwick-Strand, Chief Revenue Officer
Carrowmore Dental Group PLLC — By: Dr. Niamh Carrowmore, Managing Dentist

question: If the alumni association cancels 45 days before the event, what do they owe?
pages:
CATERING SERVICES AGREEMENT

Caterer: Saffron & Sorrel Events Ltd. ("Caterer")
Client: Ivybridge Alumni Association ("Client")
Event: Annual Alumni Gala, Saturday 16 May 2026, Thornfield Assembly Rooms, Brackenford
Agreement Date: 10 January 2026

1. Menu and Guests. Caterer will provide a three-course plated dinner for a guaranteed minimum of 180 guests at $92 per guest, plus a cocktail reception at $18 per guest.

2. Final Guest Count. Client must confirm the final guest count no later than 10 days before the Event. The final count may not be lower than the guaranteed minimum, and Client will be charged for the final count or the actual number served, whichever is greater.

3. Deposit and Payment. A non-refundable deposit of 30% of the estimated total is due on signing. A further 50% is due 30 days before the Event, and the balance is due 3 days after the Event.

4. Service Charge. A service charge of 20% is added to all food and beverage charges. Gratuities are at Client's discretion and are not included in the service charge.

5. Cancellation. If Client cancels 90 or more days before the Event, Caterer retains the deposit only. If Client cancels between 89 and 30 days before the Event, Client owes 60% of the estimated total. If Client cancels fewer than 30 days before the Event, Client owes 100% of the estimated total.

6. Staffing. Caterer will provide one server for every 12 guests and one bartender for every 60 guests.

7. Allergies. Caterer will accommodate dietary requirements notified with the final guest count. Caterer cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment.

8. Force Majeure. Neither party is liable for failure to perform due to events beyond its reasonable control, including severe weather, fire or government order.

Saffron & Sorrel Events Ltd. — By: Leontyne Okerlund-Sorrel, Director
Ivybridge Alumni Association — By: Bartholomew Quince, Gala Chair

raw.answer: Cancelling 45 days before the Event falls in the 89-to-30-day window, so the Association owes 60% of the estimated total. As an illustration only, at the guaranteed minimum of 180 guests, 60% of the food and reception charges would be $11,880, or $14,256 if the 20% service charge counts toward the estimated total.
raw.explanation: Clause 5 (Cancellation) sets 60% of the estimated total for cancellations between 89 and 30 days before the Event, and 45 days falls in that range. The illustrative figures use the per-guest prices and 180-guest guaranteed minimum from Clause 1, with the 20% service charge from Clause 4 shown as a variant. The agreement does not define the 'estimated total', so these figures are not stated amounts.
not_stated: How the 'estimated total' is calculated, including whether it includes the 20% service charge or is based on the 180-guest minimum.
Whether the non-refundable 30% deposit already paid is credited against the 60% owed.
When the cancellation amount must be paid.

The Firm will (a) prepare the Client's federal and state corporate income tax returns for the fiscal year ending 31 December 2024; (b) prepare quarterly sales tax filings for four (4) quarters; and (c) provide up to twelve (12) hours of general tax advisory consultation per calendar year (the "Advisory Hours").

Please sign and return a copy of this letter to confirm your agreement.

Harlow & Finch Advisory LLP

EXAMPLE CONSULTING AGREEMENT

This Consulting Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 10 June 2025 (the "Effective Date") by and between Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC, a limited liability company with offices at 19 Gantry Lane, Millhaven ("Consultant"), and Tessaline Outdoor Co., a corporation with offices at 640 Ridgeback Avenue, Cedar Hollow ("Company").

1. Definitions.
1.1 "Deliverables" means the reports, models and presentations described in Exhibit A.
1.2 "Project" means the market-entry assessment for the Company's proposed line of lightweight camping stoves.
1.3 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Cedar Hollow.

2. Services. Consultant shall perform the Project and deliver the Deliverables in accordance with the timeline in Exhibit A. Consultant shall assign a lead consultant who will devote not less than 20 hours per week to the Project.

3. Term. This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of six (6) months (the "Initial Term"). Thereafter it renews automatically for successive three (3) month periods unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 15 Business Days before the end of the then-current term.

4. Minimum Commitment. The Company may not terminate this Agreement for convenience during the first three (3) months of the Initial Term. After the third month, the Company may terminate for convenience on 20 Business Days' written notice.

5. Termination for Cause. Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure the breach within 10 Business Days after receiving written notice of it.

6. Fees. The Company shall pay Consultant a monthly fee of $14,500 (the "Monthly Fee"). In addition, upon acceptance of the final Deliverable the Company shall pay a success fee equal to 4% of the first-year projected revenue stated in the accepted market-entry model, capped at $40,000.

7. Payment Terms. Consultant shall invoice the Monthly Fee on the first Business Day of each month. The Company shall pay each invoice within 30 days of receipt. Late payments bear interest at 1.5% per month, and Consultant may suspend the Services if any invoice remains unpaid more than 45 days after receipt.

8. Expenses. The Company shall reimburse reasonable travel expenses pre-approved in writing. Airfare shall be economy class for flights under five (5) hours.

9. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep the other party's Confidential Information confidential for a period of three (3) years after termination of this Agreement. This obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party.

10. Intellectual Property. Upon full payment of all fees, all rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Company. Consultant retains ownership of its pre-existing methodologies, templates and tools, and grants the Company a perpetual, non-exclusive licence to use them as embedded in the Deliverables.

11. Non-Solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other party who worked on the Project.

12. Insurance. Consultant shall maintain professional liability insurance with a limit of not less than $1,000,000 per claim.

13. Limitation of Liability. Except for breaches of Section 9, neither party's total liability under this Agreement shall exceed the fees paid in the six (6) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

14. Governing Law and Venue. This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Eastmarch. The courts located in Millhaven shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

15. Notices. Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt to the addresses set out above.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.

Brindlewick Strategy Partners LLC — By: Odalys Brindlewick, Principal
Tessaline Outdoor Co. — By: Marten Tessaline, President

SAMPLE COMMERCIAL LEASE

This Commercial Lease (the "Lease") is dated 1 April 2025 and is made between Gravenhurst Property Holdings LLC ("Landlord") and Marigold Lantern Café LLC ("Tenant").

ARTICLE 1 — BASIC TERMS
1.1 Premises: Unit 4B, 112 Fennimore Street, Port Avalon, comprising approximately 1,850 rentable square feet (the "Premises").
1.2 Term: Five (5) years, commencing 1 May 2025 (the "Commencement Date") and ending 30 April 2030.
1.3 Base Rent: $5,550 per month for Lease Years 1 and 2; $5,790 per month for Lease Years 3 and 4; and $6,020 per month for Lease Year 5.
1.4 Security Deposit: $11,100.
1.5 Permitted Use: operation of a café serving food and non-alcoholic beverages for on-site and take-away consumption.

ARTICLE 2 — RENT
2.1 Payment. Base Rent is payable in advance on the first day of each calendar month without demand, deduction or set-off.
2.2 Late Charge. If any installment of Base Rent is not received within five (5) days after its due date, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to 5% of the overdue amount. Any amount remaining unpaid for more than 30 days shall also bear interest at 10% per annum.
2.3 Rent Abatement. Provided Tenant is not in default, Base Rent for the first two (2) full calendar months of the Term shall be abated.
2.4 Operating Expenses. In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay its Proportionate Share of Operating Expenses, which is 12.4%. Landlord shall provide an annual reconciliation statement within 120 days after the end of each calendar year.

ARTICLE 3 — SECURITY DEPOSIT
3.1 Landlord shall hold the Security Deposit as security for Tenant's performance. Landlord may apply the Security Deposit to cure any default, and Tenant shall restore the amount so applied within ten (10) days after written demand.
3.2 Return. Landlord shall return the Security Deposit, less any lawful deductions, within 45 days after the expiration of the Term and Tenant's surrender of the Premises.

ARTICLE 4 — USE AND COMPLIANCE
4.1 Tenant shall use the Premises only for the Permitted Use and shall comply with all applicable laws.
4.2 Operating Hours. Tenant shall keep the Premises open to the public at least six (6) days per week.
4.3 Signage. Tenant may install exterior signage at its own cost, subject to Landlord's prior written approval of the design.

ARTICLE 5 — MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS
5.1 Landlord shall maintain the roof, foundation, structural walls and the building's main electrical and plumbing lines up to the point of entry into the Premises.
5.2 Tenant shall maintain the interior of the Premises, including fixtures, kitchen equipment and the dedicated HVAC unit serving the Premises, and shall keep a service contract for the HVAC unit with a licensed contractor.
5.3 Alterations. Tenant shall not make alterations costing more than $7,500 in the aggregate without Landlord's prior written consent.

ARTICLE 6 — INSURANCE
6.1 Tenant shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 in the aggregate, naming Landlord as additional insured.

ARTICLE 7 — ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING
7.1 Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet any part of the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord shall not unreasonably withhold.

ARTICLE 8 — RENEWAL OPTION
8.1 Tenant has one (1) option to renew the Term for an additional five (5) years, exercisable by written notice delivered not less than 180 days and not more than 365 days before the expiration of the Term. Base Rent for the renewal term shall be the then-prevailing market rent, but not less than the Base Rent in effect during the final Lease Year.

ARTICLE 9 — DEFAULT
9.1 It is an Event of Default if Tenant fails to pay rent within ten (10) days after written notice of non-payment, or fails to cure any other breach within thirty (30) days after written notice.

ARTICLE 10 — EARLY TERMINATION
10.1 Tenant may terminate this Lease effective on the last day of Lease Year 3 by giving Landlord at least nine (9) months' prior written notice and paying a termination fee equal to three (3) months of the Base Rent then in effect.

ARTICLE 11 — MISCELLANEOUS
11.1 This Lease is governed by the laws of the State of New Carthage.
11.2 Notices shall be sent by certified mail or recognized overnight courier to the addresses on the signature page.

1.1 "Equipment" means two (2) KX-40 tracked excavators and one (1) TH-17 telehandler, each as further described in Schedule 1.

5.1 The hire charge is £620 per week for each KX-40 excavator and £480 per week for the TH-17 telehandler.

6.1 The Hirer shall report any breakdown to the Owner by telephone on the day it occurs. The Owner shall repair or replace a broken-down item as soon as practicable, and no hire charge shall accrue for any full day on which the item is unusable due to a breakdown not caused by the Hirer.

7.1 Risk in the Equipment passes to the Hirer on delivery to the Site and remains with the Hirer until the Equipment is returned to the Owner's depot.
7.2 Unless the damage waiver charge applies, the Hirer shall insure the Equipment for its full replacement value against loss, theft and damage.

8.1 The Owner may terminate the hire and recover the Equipment if the Hirer fails to pay any sum within fourteen (14) days of its due date.

The Owner carries on the business of hiring construction plant. The Hirer requires plant for the Saltmarsh Bypass project and has agreed to hire the Equipment on the terms below.

1.4 "Site" means the Saltmarsh Bypass works compound, Calderra West.

5.2 Each item of Equipment is subject to a minimum hire period of four (4) weeks; if an item is returned earlier, the Hirer shall pay hire charges as if it had been hired for four (4) weeks.
5.3 Delivery is charged at £185 per trip and collection at £210 per trip, with a surcharge of £95 for any delivery or collection outside Normal Hours.
5.4 A damage waiver charge of 8% of the hire charges applies to all Equipment unless the Hirer provides evidence of its own plant insurance acceptable to the Owner.
5.5 Hire charges include up to 40 engine hours per item per week; engine hours above that allowance are charged at £14 per hour, measured by the machine's hour meter.
5.6 All charges in this Agreement are exclusive of VAT, which shall be added at 20% to every charge, including the damage waiver charge.

6. BREAKDOWN
6.1 The Hirer shall report any breakdown to the Owner by telephone on the day it occurs. The Owner shall repair or replace a broken-down item as soon as practicable, and no hire charge shall accrue for any full day on which the item is unusable due to a breakdown not caused by the Hirer.

7.1 Risk in the Equipment passes to the Hirer on delivery to the Site and remains with the Hirer until the Equipment is returned to the Owner's depot.

8.1 The Owner may terminate the hire and recover the Equipment if the Hirer fails to pay any sum within fourteen (14) days of its due date.

This Schedule is superseded by clause 5 and is retained for reference only. It has no contractual effect.

This Subscription Services Agreement is entered into on 9 March 2026 by Lumora Cloud Systems Inc., a corporation organised under the laws of the State of Ferrisport ("Lumora"), and Dovecote Veterinary Group LLC ("Customer").

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Authorised User" means an individual employee or contractor of Customer who is issued login credentials for the Platform.
1.2 "Platform" means Lumora's hosted practice-management software known as PawLedger.
1.3 "Subscription Term" means twenty-four (24) months from the Effective Date of 1 April 2026.
1.4 "Monthly Fee" means one-twelfth of the Annual Subscription Fee.

2. SUBSCRIPTION AND FEES
2.1 The Annual Subscription Fee is $54,000, invoiced annually in advance and payable within thirty (30) days of invoice.
2.2 The Annual Subscription Fee includes up to 150 Authorised Users. Additional Authorised Users may be added at $18 per user per month; Read-Only Users are charged at $6 per user per month.

3. SERVICE LEVELS
3.1 Lumora shall make the Platform available at least 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, excluding Scheduled Maintenance notified at least 48 hours in advance.
3.2 If availability in a month falls below 99.9%, Customer shall receive a service credit equal to 5% of the Monthly Fee for each full 0.1 percentage point by which availability falls below 99.9%, up to a maximum credit of 25% of the Monthly Fee for that month.
3.3 Service credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability and shall be applied against the next invoice.

4. DATA
4.1 Customer retains all rights in Customer Data. Lumora shall process Customer Data only to provide the Platform.
4.2 Lumora shall maintain industry-standard technical and organisational security measures, including encryption of Customer Data at rest and in transit.
4.3 Following expiry or termination, Customer may export Customer Data for thirty (30) days, after which Lumora shall delete it within a further sixty (60) days.

5. TERM AND TERMINATION
5.1 This Agreement continues for the Subscription Term. Customer may terminate for convenience with effect from the end of the Subscription Term by giving at least sixty (60) days' written notice; fees paid in advance are non-refundable except as stated in clause 5.2.
5.2 Either party may terminate for material breach not cured within thirty (30) days of notice; if Customer so terminates, Lumora shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after termination.
5.3 Lumora may increase fees at renewal by no more than 6%, on at least ninety (90) days' notice.

question: A Ridgeway temp with a Pay Rate of $25/hour works 46 hours in one Work Week at Solvane. What does Ridgeway bill for that week?
pages:
TEMPORARY STAFFING SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Agreement is made effective 5 January 2026 between Ridgeway Talent Partners Inc. ("Ridgeway") and Solvane Logistics Corp. ("Client").

Background
Client operates distribution centers in Tullwater and East Brannock and wishes to engage temporary warehouse associates supplied by Ridgeway.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Temporary Worker" means an individual employed by Ridgeway and assigned to perform work for Client.
1.2 "Pay Rate" means the hourly wage Ridgeway pays a Temporary Worker.
1.3 "Bill Rate" means the Pay Rate multiplied by 1.42, representing a markup of 42%.
1.4 "Work Week" means Sunday 00:00 to Saturday 23:59.

2. ASSIGNMENTS
2.1 Each shift shall be for a minimum of four (4) hours; if Client releases a Temporary Worker early, Client shall be billed for four (4) hours.
2.2 Client shall provide site-specific safety training before the first shift.

3. BILLING
3.1 Hours worked by a Temporary Worker in excess of forty (40) in any Work Week shall be billed at 1.5 times the Bill Rate.
3.2 Temporary Workers shall record hours on Ridgeway's timesheet system. Client shall approve or dispute each timesheet within two (2) Business Days of submission, failing which the timesheet shall be deemed approved.
3.3 Ridgeway shall invoice weekly and Client shall pay each invoice within fifteen (15) days of the invoice date.
3.4 Pre-assignment screening is charged per Temporary Worker as follows: background check $65, drug screen $40 and E-Verify check $12.

4. CONVERSION
4.1 If Client employs or engages a Temporary Worker directly (other than through Ridgeway), Client shall pay a conversion fee calculated on the worker's first-year base salary as follows: (a) 20% if the worker has completed fewer than 520 hours on assignment; (b) 10% if the worker has completed 520 hours or more but fewer than 1,040 hours; and (c) no fee once the worker has completed 1,040 hours.
4.2 Conversion fees are payable within thirty (30) days of the worker's start date with Client.

5. NON-SOLICITATION AND TERM
5.1 Neither party shall solicit the other's internal staff for twelve (12) months after termination.
5.2 This Agreement continues until terminated by either party on thirty (30) days' written notice.

raw.answer: Ridgeway bills $1,739.50 for the week. That is 40 hours at the $35.50 Bill Rate ($1,420.00) plus 6 overtime hours at 1.5 times the Bill Rate, or $53.25 an hour ($319.50).
raw.explanation: Clause 1.3 sets the Bill Rate at the Pay Rate multiplied by 1.42, so a $25 Pay Rate gives a $35.50 Bill Rate. This Agreement is made effective 5 January 2026 between Ridgeway Talent Partners Inc. ("Ridgeway") and Solvane Logistics Corp. ("Client").

Background
Client operates distribution centers in Tullwater and East Brannock and wishes to engage temporary warehouse associates supplied by Ridgeway.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Temporary Worker" means an individual employed by Ridgeway and assigned to perform work for Client.
1.2 "Pay Rate" means the hourly wage Ridgeway pays a Temporary Worker.
1.3 "Bill Rate" means the Pay Rate multiplied by 1.42, representing a markup of 42%.
1.4 "Work Week" means Sunday 00:00 to Saturday 23:59.

2. ASSIGNMENTS
2.1 Each shift shall be for a minimum of four (4) hours; if Client releases a Temporary Worker early, Client shall be billed for four (4) hours.

3.1 Hours worked by a Temporary Worker in excess of forty (40) in any Work Week shall be billed at 1.5 times the Bill Rate.

1. Definitions

3.1 The Recipient shall use Confidential Information only for the Purpose and disclose it only to employees and advisers who need to know it and are bound by equivalent obligations.

3.1 The Licence Fee is £85,000, payable as to 50% on signature and 50% on installation.
3.2 Annual Maintenance Fees are 18% of the Licence Fee, payable annually in advance from the date of installation, and may be increased on each anniversary by no more than 4% over the previous year's Maintenance Fees.

4. Support
4.1 Maintenance includes Updates and telephone and e-mail support from 08:30 to 17:30 on Business Days.
4.2 The Licensor shall respond to Severity 1 support requests within two (2) Business Hours and to all other requests within one (1) Business Day.

5.1 The Licensor warrants that, for ninety (90) days from installation, the Software will perform materially in accordance with its Documentation.
5.2 The Licensee's sole remedy for breach of clause 5.1 is correction of the non-conformity or, if the Licensor cannot correct it within thirty (30) days, a refund of the Licence Fee against return of the Software.

6.1 The Licensor may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and on not less than ten (10) Business Days' notice, audit the Licensee's use of the Software.
6.2 If an audit reveals that the Licensee has underpaid fees by more than 5%, the Licensee shall pay the shortfall and the reasonable costs of the audit; otherwise the Licensee shall pay only the shortfall and the Licensor shall bear the costs of the audit.

9.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Duchy of Marrowby.

pages:

This Agreement is made on 6 November 2025 between Saffron Lantern Events Ltd ("Organiser") and Marlowe-Quist Pharma Ltd ("Client").

The Client is holding its Northern Medical Affairs Summit at Ashcombe Hall, Thornleigh, on 14 and 15 May 2026 (the "Event"), and the Organiser will manage venue hire, catering, audio-visual services and delegate registration.

1. Delegate Numbers and Charges
1.1 The Client guarantees a minimum of 220 delegates per Event day (the "Minimum Numbers").
1.2 The day delegate rate is £74 per delegate per Event day, covering venue hire, refreshments, buffet lunch and standard AV, and the Client shall be charged for the greater of actual attendance and the Minimum Numbers on each Event day.
1.3 The Client may reduce the Minimum Numbers by up to 10% by written notice given no later than thirty (30) days before the Event.
1.4 An enhanced AV package (LED wall, two camera operators and live streaming) is available at £2,950 for the whole Event.
1.5 All charges are subject to VAT at 20%.

2. Payment
2.1 A deposit of 30% of the Estimated Event Price is payable on signature; the balance is payable within fourteen (14) days after the Event.
2.2 "Estimated Event Price" means the Minimum Numbers multiplied by the day delegate rate and the number of Event days, plus any optional packages booked, exclusive of VAT.

3.1 If the Client cancels the Event, it shall pay the following cancellation charge, as a percentage of the Estimated Event Price: (a) more than 120 days before the Event: 25%; (b) between 60 and 120 days before the Event: 50%; (c) less than 60 days before the Event: 100%.
3.2 Any deposit paid shall be credited against the cancellation charge.

4. Organiser Obligations
4.1 The Organiser shall send the Client a final run sheet for the Event in good time before the Event and shall staff a registration desk from 07:30 on each Event day.

5. Liability
5.1 The Organiser's liability is limited to the total charges paid by the Client under this Agreement.

raw.answer: Marlowe-Quist is charged for the 220-delegate minimum on each day, not the 180 who attended. That comes to £32,560 before VAT, plus £6,512 VAT, so the total delegate charge is £39,072.
